transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just feel... I don't know, wound up almost all day. It's like my body is constantly bracing for something. Even when I’m just sitting at my computer for work. Actually, I just got one of those standing desk converters because I thought maybe it was my chair causing it? I do database management, so I'm staring at screens for eight hours, and my company just rolled out this new software update that completely changed the dashboard. It took me three days just to figure out how to run my usual reports, and don't even get me started on our IT help desk, they literally never answer their tickets on time. It's ridiculous. But... um, what was I saying? Oh, right. It's just that even when I'm off the computer and just trying to relax after dinner, I still have that weird, tense, braced feeling.
Do you experience any physical pain when you're feeling wound up and tense?

No, not really pain, just... tightness, I guess? Like my shoulders are practically up by my ears. My husband, Frank, he always tells me I need to get a massage, but honestly, who has the time? Plus, the last time I went to a massage therapist, she played this awful, plinky-plinky pan flute music the entire hour. It was supposed to be relaxing, but it just reminded me of being on hold with the cable company. We were trying to get our internet upgraded last month because Frank wanted to stream some new fishing show in 4K, and I swear I was on the phone for two hours listening to that exact same music. And then they didn't even send the right router! But anyway... no, no actual pain, just that really tight feeling.
Do you find that this tense, braced feeling happens at specific times or in specific situations?

No, not really. I haven't noticed any sort of pattern with it. It just happens whenever. Like, I could just be standing in the kitchen making breakfast. Frank always wants his eggs over easy, which is fine, but our favorite skillet is completely scratched up. I told him we needed a new one when we were at Target last weekend, but he got completely sidetracked in the garden section. They had all their patio furniture on clearance, and suddenly he's measuring things and talking about replacing our deck chairs. Which makes no sense, because we don't even use the deck! The neighbor's dog barks at the fence every single time we step outside. It’s a beagle, and it has that awful, loud howl... wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, situations. Yeah, no, I don't think there's a specific time it happens. It's just kind of there.
Do you feel more wound up or tense when you're around other people, like at work or in social gatherings?

Not really... I mean, I don't think being around people makes it any worse. It's just the same whether I'm alone or with a group. Honestly, we don't even have that many social gatherings anymore. Frank's sister used to host this big potluck every Fourth of July, but she moved to Arizona two years ago. Said she couldn't take the winters here anymore, which I get, but now she complains about the heat! She actually sent us a picture of a thermometer on her patio that read 115 degrees. Can you imagine? I would just melt. Anyway, my company did have a holiday party last December at this fancy Italian place downtown. The food was okay, but the parking was an absolute nightmare. We had to park three blocks away and it was sleeting. By the time we got inside, my nice suede boots were ruined. I tried that protective spray on them, but it didn't do a thing... but, um, no, people don't seem to make the tense feeling any different. It's just always sort of humming in the background.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you have that tense, braced feeling?

Oh, absolutely. It’s like my mind just won't ever turn off. It just keeps bouncing from one concern to another. I’ll be sitting there with my shoulders practically glued to my ears, and I start worrying about my sister down in Arecibo. She lives right near where that massive radio telescope used to be before it collapsed a few years ago. It was all over the news, such a shame. They filmed a James Bond movie there once, you know. Pierce Brosnan, I think? Or maybe it was Jodie Foster in that alien movie. She has such good hair in that. 

But anyway, I'll be worrying about her, and then my brain just jumps to wondering if I missed something at the office. They just updated our entire network interface last week, and the new dashboard is completely counter-intuitive. The font is so small I had to increase my screen zoom to 125%, and it messes up the formatting on all my spreadsheets. So I worry about that, and then I'm suddenly worrying about Frank driving home in rush hour traffic, especially with the construction on I-95. And then it's my church commitments, or whether the water bill went through... I just find myself constantly preparing for all these problems that haven’t even happened yet. Like I'm always bracing for a disaster, but half the time I don't even know what disaster I'm supposed to be looking out for.
Do you think your tense feeling is related to something physical going on in your body?

Physical? Like a medical issue? No, I don't really think so. I mean, I went to my primary care doctor for my annual physical a few months ago, and everything looked fine. Well, my cholesterol was a tiny bit high, but my doctor said I just need to eat more oatmeal. I tried buying those steel-cut oats because they're supposed to be better for you, but they take absolutely forever to cook. Who has thirty minutes to stand at the stove and stir oatmeal before work? 

Frank bought this fancy rice cooker online that supposedly has a special oatmeal setting, but the instructions were completely in Japanese. He spent three hours on YouTube trying to figure out how to program the timer, and he still managed to burn the oats to the bottom of the pot. It took me two days to scrub the burnt smell out of the kitchen. I ended up having to use baking soda and vinegar, which honestly works so much better than any of those expensive chemical sprays they sell at the store. Plus it's better for the environment, you know? 

But, um... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, my body. No, I don't think the tenseness is from anything physical going on with me. My health is pretty normal.
Do you ever have periods where you feel completely relaxed and the tense feeling goes away?

Not really... I mean, I can't remember the last time I felt completely relaxed. Even when I try to unwind, it's just there. Frank and I tried to take a weekend trip up to a bed and breakfast in Vermont last fall, thinking that would help. We went during peak foliage season, which is just beautiful up there. The reds and oranges are incredible, like a painting. But the traffic on the interstate was unbelievable. All those "leaf peepers," they call them. We were stuck behind this huge RV with Florida plates for almost two hours. I don't know why someone would drive an RV all the way from Florida just to look at trees. 

Anyway, the B&B was supposed to be this quiet, quaint little place, but they had this antique grandfather clock in the hallway right outside our room. It chimed every single hour, and on the half-hour too! I barely slept a wink the whole weekend. I kept waiting for the next chime. Frank slept right through it, of course. He could sleep through a marching band in our living room. He actually fell asleep during my niece's piano recital last month. She was playing Beethoven, very aggressively too, and he just nodded right off in the second row. 

So, no, even when I'm supposed to be relaxing, I'm just... I'm still wound up. It never really goes away.
Have you ever had a period of time, say a few months, where you didn't worry about things as much as you do now?

Well, not recently, no. I mean, this whole thing... it's been going on for about thirteen months now. It really started getting bad when my sister down in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. She's been having a tough time, and it's just so hard being far away. I actually looked into flights down there a few months ago, thinking maybe I could just go for a long weekend and help her sort some things out. But the prices were absolutely ridiculous. I don't know what's going on with the airlines lately, but they want an arm and a leg just for a standard economy seat, and they don't even give you peanuts anymore! 

Frank used to travel for work all the time back in the nineties, and he'd always bring back those little bags of honey-roasted peanuts. They were so good. Now you're lucky if they toss you a tiny bag of pretzels that taste like cardboard. And they charge you extra if you want to bring a bag that's bigger than a purse! It's just highway robbery, really. I ended up not booking the flight because I just couldn't justify the cost, and then I spent the next three weeks feeling guilty about not going. So... yeah, about thirteen months of just constant worrying.
Is there anything in particular that you think triggers your worrying or is it more about anything and everything in general?

Well, it's really everything, honestly. It's not just one thing. My mind just keeps going from one concern to another. Like, I'll be worrying about my sister down in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm stressing about whether I missed an email at the office. We just switched to this new software system at work, and it's an absolute nightmare. They brought in these consultants who looked like they were barely out of high school to train us. One of them, I swear he was wearing sneakers with a suit. Who does that? And they talk so fast, using all these buzzwords like "synergy" and "bandwidth." I told Frank, my bandwidth is completely full just trying to figure out how to log in! 

And Frank, oh, he works on the other side of town, and the traffic on Route 9 is just terrible. I sit there worrying about him driving home, especially when it rains. People around here forget how to drive the second a drop of water hits the windshield. Then I start thinking about my commitments at the church, and the electric bill... did you know the electric company raised their rates again? They sent this little insert in the bill explaining it, printed in font so small you need a magnifying glass to read it. I actually had to use Frank's reading glasses, which he always leaves on the kitchen counter instead of putting them back in their case. 

But anyway, yeah, it's just... everything. I find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet. It just never stops.
Do you feel like you can control your worrying when it starts?

I try, I really do. I'll be sitting at my desk, and I'll tell myself, "Daniela, enough, focus on this report." But then one small thought pops up, and it just turns into five more. Before I know it, I've spent half an hour checking messages or replaying what could go wrong instead of actually working. It's like my brain just hijacks me. 

Speaking of my desk, they just replaced all our office chairs last week. Supposedly they're "ergonomic," but I swear it feels like sitting on a bag of potatoes. The lumbar support hits me right in the middle of my back instead of the lower back, and there's this weird lever underneath that I keep kicking with my heel. My coworker, Susan—she sits in the cubicle next to me—she spent an entire hour trying to adjust hers and ended up lowering it so far she looked like a child sitting at the grown-ups' table. She's so short anyway, she really didn't need to go any lower. She actually brings a little footstool from home just so her feet touch the ground. 

But anyway, to answer your question, no. I really can't stop it once it gets going. It just spirals.
Do you think your worrying is excessive, considering the actual problems you're facing?

Well, I suppose part of me knows it is. Like, Frank always tells me I make mountains out of molehills. But in the moment, it all feels completely justified, you know? Like I have to figure it all out right then and there. 

Frank's actually been saying that a lot lately, especially since he started that new hobby of his. He decided he wanted to get into woodworking. Woodworking! At his age. He went out and bought all these expensive tools—a table saw, a router, clamps in every size imaginable. He set up this whole workshop in the garage, which means I have to park my car in the driveway now. And you know how the oak tree in our front yard drops those little acorns everywhere? They get stuck right in the windshield wipers. I had to replace the wiper blades just last month because they got all torn up. The guy at the auto parts store tried to upsell me on these "premium silicone" ones, claiming they last twice as long. I told him, "Listen, I just need them to wipe the rain off, I'm not driving through a hurricane." 

But yeah, I guess... I guess maybe I do worry more than I should. It just feels like if I don't worry about it, who will?
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your ability to do your job or enjoy activities you normally like to do?

Well, I'm still getting my work done, and I'm still showing up for my commitments at the church and everything with the family. But... it definitely takes me longer to finish my reports now. I find myself double-checking things way more than I used to. Like yesterday, I must have read over the same spreadsheet four times before I sent it to my manager. 

Speaking of my manager, he just got back from this two-week vacation in Italy. Must be nice, right? He brought back all these pictures of him and his wife eating gelato in front of the Colosseum. He spent twenty minutes at the staff meeting just talking about the pasta. Apparently, they don't use as much sauce over there, it's more about the noodles. He brought back some sort of fancy olive oil for the office kitchen, but nobody wants to use it because the bottle is so pretty. It's got this little hand-painted lemon on the front. I told Susan, "We're just going to end up staring at it until it goes rancid." 

But anyway, yeah... the worrying does get in the way sometimes. Like I said, the work takes longer. And I've noticed I've been a bit snappy lately. I've actually had to apologize a few times for sounding short with Frank and my sister. I just get so wound up in my own head that when they ask me a simple question, I kind of bite their heads off.
Do you feel like your worrying is affecting your relationships with family and friends?

I don't really think so? I mean, I know I just said I've been a little snappy with Frank and my sister lately, but it's not like we're having big blow-out fights or anything. I haven't really noticed it causing any deep problems between us. 

Speaking of my sister, she actually just came over for dinner on Sunday. She adopted this new rescue dog—a Golden Retriever mix, I think she said. His name is Buster. Sweetest thing, but oh my goodness, the shedding! I had to spend an hour vacuuming the living room rug after they left. I have one of those Dyson vacuums, the cordless ones? Frank bought it for me for Christmas two years ago. At first I was a little offended—I mean, who buys their wife a vacuum cleaner for Christmas, right?—but honestly, it's the best thing ever. It has this little green laser on the front that shows you exactly where the dust is on the hardwood floors. It's actually horrifying how much dust it highlights. You think your house is clean, and then you turn that laser on and it looks like a fuzzy desert landscape. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, my family and friends. Yeah, no, I don't really have much to say there. I think they just know how I am, so it's all just kind of normal for us.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes and includes symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling?

No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, my heart races if I drink way too much coffee, but not from fear or anything. 

Actually, Frank just bought this ridiculously complicated espresso machine for the kitchen. It literally looks like a spaceship sitting on the counter. It has all these pressure dials and a steam wand that makes this awful screeching noise when he uses it. He spent half of Saturday watching internet videos just to learn how to pack the coffee grounds perfectly. He made me a cappuccino the other morning using some oat milk my niece left in our fridge. I really don't understand the whole oat milk trend, it just tastes like leftover cereal water to me. But I drank it to be polite, and I swear he put three shots of espresso in it. My heart was definitely pounding after that! I ended up having to reorganize the entire linen closet just to burn off the jitters. I found pillowcases in there from when the kids were in middle school. 

But, um, anyway... what was the question? Oh, the sudden fear. No, no sudden intense fear or sweating out of nowhere. Just my usual worrying.
Is your worrying usually about a specific issue or problem, or is it more general, covering many different things?

Well, it's definitely not just one thing. It's more like my mind just keeps going from one concern to another, constantly. Like, I'll be worrying about my sister down in Arecibo, and then suddenly I'm stressing about whether I missed something important on a report at the office, or if Frank is going to be okay driving home in the rain, or if I'm doing enough for my church commitments, or if the bills are all paid. I just find myself preparing for problems that haven't even happened yet. 

Speaking of my sister in Arecibo, she actually just sent me this huge box of pasteles last week. Have you ever had them? They are so much work to make. You have to grate the green bananas and the yautía, and the pork has to marinate forever. She wraps them in these banana leaves that she actually grows in her own backyard. It's incredible. But the shipping! Oh my goodness, she had to pay for overnight shipping on dry ice so they wouldn't spoil, and the box was so heavy I could barely lift it off the porch. Frank tried to help me and almost dropped it on his foot. He was wearing those terrible rubber clogs he refuses to throw away. I keep telling him they're a tripping hazard, especially with the tread completely worn off the bottom, but he just says they're his "yard shoes." 

But anyway... yeah, the worrying. It's just a bunch of different things all the time. It never really stops on just one topic.
Do you feel like your worrying is making it hard for you to enjoy the things you used to enjoy?

I don't think so? I mean, I still like doing things, I just... I might be a little more distracted while I'm doing them, I guess. But I still enjoy my hobbies and everything. 

Actually, I just started a new cross-stitch pattern last month. It's this beautiful old farmhouse with a wrap-around porch and these tiny little sunflowers in the front yard. The pattern is huge, though. It takes up almost the whole dining room table when I lay it out. I had to buy a special magnifying lamp just to see the stitches because my eyes aren't what they used to be. I got it at that craft store over on Route 9, you know the one? They were having a huge clearance sale because they're remodeling the whole plaza. It's about time, too. The parking lot there has had these massive potholes for at least five years. Last winter, Frank hit one so hard it knocked the hubcap right off his tire, and we never did find it. It was a rental car, too, because his transmission was getting fixed. We had to pay this ridiculous fee when we returned it. 

But um, what were you asking? Oh, enjoying things. Yeah, no, I still enjoy my cross-stitching and everything. I just worry while I'm doing it.
Do you feel like your worrying is affecting your overall quality of life?

I mean, I'm still functioning, you know? I'm getting all my work done, and I'm still showing up for my family and all my church commitments. But... I guess it is affecting things a little bit. It definitely takes me a lot longer to finish my reports at work now. I just find myself double-checking things way more than I used to. I'll read over an email three times before I hit send, just to make sure I didn't make some stupid mistake. 

Actually, speaking of emails, our IT department just rolled out this new security system last week, and it is driving everyone completely crazy. You have to use this authenticator app on your phone every single time you log in, and half the time the app doesn't even send the notification. So you're just sitting there staring at the screen, waiting. My coworker, Brenda—she sits in the cubicle next to me—she got locked out of her account for an entire morning because she entered the code wrong too many times. She was so flustered. Brenda's usually so put together, too. She always brings these amazing little bento boxes for lunch with perfectly cut vegetables and little rice balls shaped like pandas. I keep meaning to ask her where she gets those tiny little nori punchers to make the panda faces. 

But, oh, right, my quality of life. Yeah, the double-checking takes up a lot of time. And I guess... I have had to apologize a few times lately for snapping at Frank or my sister. I just get so wound up in my head that I end up sounding really short with the people I care about. So, I suppose it is taking a bit of a toll, even if I'm still getting everything done.
Are you finding it increasingly difficult to concentrate on your daily tasks due to your worrying?

Concentrating? Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I can still focus on what I need to do just fine. Like right now, we're doing this massive data migration at work—moving all our legacy files over to a new cloud server—and I have to map all these database fields, which takes a lot of focus. 

They actually just gave us all new dual monitors for the project. They're those really wide, curved ones? It takes up my entire desk. The IT guy who came to set it up, Terry, he was telling me about how his youngest daughter just started college out in Ohio and she's already wanting to change her major from pre-med to art history. I told him, you know, at eighteen, they really don't know what they want to do yet. My niece did the exact same thing a few years ago, except she dropped out of business school to do culinary arts. She makes these incredible macarons now, though. She uses real vanilla bean paste, not the cheap extract, and you can really taste the difference. The last batch she brought over was Earl Grey and lavender... they were just beautiful. They have these perfect little "feet" on the bottom, which she says is the hardest part to get right when you're baking them. 

But, um... what were you asking me? Oh, concentrating. Right. No, I haven't really noticed any problems with my concentration. I just have all that worrying going on in the background while I work.
Do you think your worrying has been present for most of every day for the past several months?

Well, let's see... most of every day... yeah, I'd say so. It's been pretty constant. I think it really started getting bad about thirteen months ago. That's when my sister down in Arecibo started needing a lot more help from the family. She's got this beautiful little house right near the observatory—well, what's left of it, anyway. It was so sad when the telescope collapsed a few years back. We used to go visit it when we were kids, and it was just this massive, incredible structure nestled right into the hills. 

Anyway, the humidity down there is just relentless on a house, and she's been dealing with all these plumbing issues lately. The pipes in those older homes just can't handle it. She had to have a plumber come out three times in one week last month because the guest bathroom kept backing up. The guy who came out, Hector, he's actually the cousin of my brother-in-law's mechanic. Small island, you know? Everyone knows everyone. He was telling her that the whole street needs their main lines replaced, but the municipality keeps dragging their feet on the permits. 

But um, what was the question? Oh, how long it's been going on. Yeah, about thirteen months, ever since she started needing all that extra help from us. It's just been a constant worry every day since then.
